rules.label: FPL 0-100%: Free care (100% discount)
rules.quote: Patients whose family income is at or below 100% of the FPL are eligible to receive free care.

rules.label: FPL 101-125%: Up to 80% discount
rules.quote: Patients whose family income is over 100% and below 125% of the FPL would be eligible for up to an 80% discount.

rules.label: FPL 126-150%: Up to 60% discount
rules.quote: Patients whose family income is over 125% and below 150% of the FPL would be eligible for up to a 60% discount.

rules.label: FPL 151-200%: Up to 40% discount
rules.quote: Patients whose family income is over 150% and below 200% of the FPL would be eligible for up to a 40% discount.

rules.label: FPL 201-250%: Up to 20% discount
rules.quote: Patients who family income is over 200% and below 250% of the FPL would be eligible for up to a 20% discount.

rules.label: FPL above 250%: Case-by-case for catastrophic illness or medical indigence
rules.quote: Patients whose family income exceeds 250% of the FPL will generally not be deemed eligible for financial assistance; but, may be considered for financial assistance on a case-by-case basis based on their specific circumstances, such as catastrophic illness or medical indigence, at the discretion of RGH.

application.quote: A patient has 240 days after the date of first billing to submit data for financial assistance.

eca_not_before.quote: No extraordinary collection action will be taken before 182 days from the first bill.

notes: Policy applies to hospital, clinics, and employed providers (inpatient, ER, family practice, orthopedics by Dr. Hunter, surgery by Thompson, anesthesia by Monarch). Excludes non-employee providers: Colorado Imaging Associates radiologists, San Luis Valley Health specialists, Health One cardiology, Vascular Institute of the Rockies, surgeries by Chang and Marshall-Rodriguez.
Discounted rates shall not exceed amounts generally billed to commercially insured patients (look-back method using Medicare fee-for-service and private insurer claims).
Financial need re-evaluated every 12 months or if financial situation changes.
Application requires documentation: tax return, W-2, pay stubs (6 months), bank statements (3 months), employer letter, SSA award letter, or proof of direct deposit.
Accounts eligible for financial assistance addressed within 240 days of first bill; accounts may be considered up to 6 months prior to determination and up to 1 year after.
RGH notifies patient in writing within 30 days of completed application.
Collection activity suspended during financial assistance review; resumes if partial adjustment, non-cooperation, or ineligibility.
ECA not initiated for emergency care (emergency, inpatient, ancillary services). If account in ECA later qualifies, RGH reverses ECA.
Patients who owe balance after insurance or are higher income and do not qualify may be pursued for litigation in Colorado.
Policy complies with Colorado DSH and Colorado Hospital Discount Care rules.
Application available in English and Spanish.
Self-pay accounts outsourced; reviewed for further action if not paid or satisfactory arrangements not made.

dropped.quote: RGH will not engage in or impose extraordinary collection actions such as wage garnishments, liens on primary residences, or other legal actions for any patient without first making reasonable efforts to determine whether that patient is eligible for financial assistance under this financial assistance policy. Reasonable efforts shall include: Validating that the patient owes the unpaid bills and that all sources of third-party payment have been identified and billed by the hospital. Documentation that RGH has, or has attempted to offer the patient the opportunity to apply for financial assistance pursuant to this policy and that the patient has not complied with the hospital's application requirements. Documentation that the patient has been offered a payment plan but has not honored the terms of that plan.

notes: The policy states that patients with income exceeding 250% FPL may be considered for financial assistance on a case-by-case basis for circumstances such as catastrophic illness or medical indigence at the discretion of RGH.

The policy excludes financial assistance for physician fees or other charges from non-employee providers, listing examples such as Rocky Mountain Radiology, Aurora Denver Cardiology, Urology Associates, North Colorado Springs Foot Clinic, San Luis Valley Health, and Dr. Matthew K. Chang.
The policy specifies that the determination of financial need may be done at any point in the collection cycle and should be re-evaluated every 12 months or if the financial situation changes.

The policy requires applicants to submit a completed Financial Assistance Application with supporting documentation, including at least one of: copy of last year’s tax return, IRS Form W-2, paycheck stubs from the past six months, bank statements from the last three months, signed employer letter verifying gross monthly income for past six months, Social Security award letter, or proof of direct deposit.

Presumptive eligibility may be based on circumstances such as participation in state-funded prescription programs, homelessness, WIC, food stamp eligibility, subsidized school lunch, eligibility for unfunded state/local assistance programs (e.g., Medicaid spend-down), low-income/subsidized housing as a valid address, or patient deceased with no known estate.

The policy applies to hospital, clinics, and all employed providers including inpatient, emergency room, and family practice clinic providers (employed, contracted, agencies), orthopedics by Dr. Robert Hunter, surgery by Patrick Thompson, and anesthesia by Monarch Anesthesia.

The policy does not apply to radiologists from Colorado Imaging Associates, specialists from San Luis Valley Health (ENT, OB), Health One (Cardiology), Vascular Institute of the Rockies (vascular surgery), anesthesia/surgery by San Luis Valley Health, surgery by Mathew Chang, surgery by Amanda Marshall-Rodriguez, surgery by Dr. Silva & Dr. Lewis, and surgery by Dr. Hunter.
The policy states that RGH will follow all Colorado DSH and Colorado Hospital Discount Care rules for patients qualifying under financial assistance.

The policy includes a sliding fee scale table showing charges and discounts for inpatient (IP), emergency room (ER), and physician (Phy) services across FPL ranges, though the exact interpretation of the dollar amounts is not fully specified in the vocabulary.
